column11: Genesis 3:22: ‘And the ETERNAL God said, “Now that humankind has become like any of us, knowing good and bad, what if one should stretch out a hand and take also from the tree of life and eat, and live forever!”’ Context and connection to Machshavot Charutz: In Machshavot Charutz 7, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Genesis 3:22) to illuminate his exposition here (“for it is said: "And now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever" (Bereishis 3:22); and the Sages of blessed memory stated (Bereishis Rabbah...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the supernal levels of Thought (Machshavah), the rectification of human desire and intellect, and the inner light of the Oral Torah developed in Machshavot Charutz.
column13: And this supreme state is merited only by one who never tasted the taste of sin in his life, like Adam HaRishon prior to the sin, whose dwelling was in Gan Eden, and there he was able to eat of the Tree of Life and live forever; but after the sin he was banished from there: "lest he put forth his hand, etc." (Bereishis 3:22), for regarding this repentance did not avail him to rectify the root of the Serpent's instigation and abolish the decree of death, see [above, Siman 3].
column15: Now Adam HaRishon, being the direct handiwork of the Holy One, blessed be He, perceived clearly that without the divine Will nothing comes to pass. column11: Bereshit Rabbah 21:6: ‘“And now, he might extend his hand” – Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: This teaches that the Holy One blessed be He opened for him an opportunity for repentance. “And now” – “and now” is nothing other than repentance, as it is stated: “And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God [ask of you? Only to fear the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways…]” (Deuteronomy 10:12). But he [Adam] said: “Might [pen]” – and pen is nothing other than no. The Holy One blessed be He said: ‘Will he now extend his hand and eat from the tree of life?’ It was a rhetorical question. And if he eats, he will live forever. column15: “And now nothing will be withholden from them, which they purpose to do.” In Midrash Rabbah (38:9): This teaches that the Holy One opened for them a portal of repentance, as said: “And now (ve'atah)”—and “ve'atah” signifies repentance, as it is said (Deuteronomy 10:12): “And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear”; yet they said “No”.

column11: Bamidbar Rabbah 19:4: ‘“Who is like the wise man, and who knows the meaning of a matter?” (Ecclesiastes 8:1). “Who is like the wise man” – this is the Holy One blessed be He, in whose regard it is written: “The Lord founded the earth with wisdom” (Proverbs 3:19). “And who knows the meaning of a matter” – this is the Holy One blessed be He, who explained the Torah to Moses. “The wisdom of a man illuminates his face” (Ecclesiastes 8:1) – Rabbi Yudan said: Great is the ability of the prophets, who liken the image of the greatness On High to the form of a person, as it is stated: “I heard the voice of a man by the Ulai” (Daniel 8:16). column15: So that man should awaken the supernal Archetype from Above which enfolds all divine attributes and the supreme Will. column11: Bamidbar Rabbah 19:8: ‘A certain idolater asked Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakai: ‘These actions that you perform seem to be a type of sorcery. But the primary root of the evil inclination is purely lust, wherein Adam the First Man sinned and generated the drive of lust, from which the second drive subsequently branched.

column11: Shabbat 118b: ‘Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei: With regard to anyone who delights in the Shabbat, God gives him a boundless portion, i.e., a very large reward, as it is stated: “If you keep your feet from violating Shabbat, from pursuing your affairs on My holy day, and you call Shabbat a delight, the Lord’s holy day honored, and you honor it by not going your own way, or attending to your own matters or speaking idle words. Rabbi Yitzḥak said that the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to the Jewish people: Even if your sins are as numerous as those years [kashanim] that have proceeded continuously from the six days of Creation until now, they will become white like snow. Rava taught: What is the meaning of that which is written: “Go please and let us reason together, the Lord will say” (Isaiah 1:18)? Why does the verse say: Go please? It should have said: Come please.…’ Context and connection to Machshavot Charutz: In Machshavot Charutz 8, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Shabbat 89b) to illuminate his exposition here (“and then it will be clarified regarding all the sins of Israel that they were ordered and advancing from the six days of Creation, as written in Perek Rabbi Akiva (Shabbat 89b); meaning when...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the supernal levels of Thought (Machshavah), the rectification of human desire and intellect, and the inner light of the Oral Torah developed in Machshavot Charutz.

column11: Makkot 24a: ‘§ Rabbi Simlai taught: There were 613 mitzvot stated to Moses in the Torah, consisting of 365 prohibitions corresponding to the number of days in the solar year, and 248 positive mitzvot corresponding to the number of a person’s limbs. Rav Hamnuna said: What is the verse that alludes to this? It is written: “Moses commanded to us the Torah, an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob” (Deuteronomy 33:4). The word Torah, in terms of its numerical value [gimatriyya], is 611, the number of mitzvot that were received and taught by Moses our teacher. In addition, there are two mitzvot: “I am the Lord your God” and: “You shall have no other gods” (Exodus 20:2, 3), the first two of the Ten Commandments, that we heard from the mouth of the Almighty, for a total of 613.’ Context and connection to Machshavot Charutz: In Machshavot Charutz 8, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Makkot 24a) to illuminate his exposition here (“which is the level of Knesset Israel in this world who received the Torah directly from the mouth of the Almighty (Makkos 24a), after the manner of "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth"...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the supernal levels of Thought (Machshavah), the rectification of human desire and intellect, and the inner light of the Oral Torah developed in Machshavot Charutz.
